contracts.grain: One row per claim with status OPEN or REOPENED and reported on or before the reporting date (@AsOfDate), with paid to date, latest case reserves and incurred as at that date.

columns.name: claim_ref
columns.description: lob_code + '/' + claim_number + '/' + handler_code. It is NULL whenever handler_code is NULL, because T-SQL string concatenation returns NULL if any part is NULL (109 rows).

columns.name: policy_number
columns.description: Comes from the latest policy snapshot on or before @AsOfDate. Left join, so it can be NULL.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Filtered with IN ('OPEN','REOPENED'), but the output has 6 distinct values. A case- or space-insensitive collation is probably letting variants such as 'open' or 'Open ' through, so the Spark filter must compare the same way.

columns.name: reported_period
columns.description: yyyymm from reported_date (CONVERT style 112 cut to 6 characters).

columns.name: days_open
columns.description: Whole days from reported_date to @AsOfDate (DATEDIFF DAY).

columns.name: n_payments
columns.description: COUNT(DISTINCT payment_id) of payments dated on or before @AsOfDate.

columns.name: total_paid
columns.description: SUM of payment amounts on or before @AsOfDate, 0 if none. Legacy fan-out: payments are joined to the reserve rows (up to one per reserve type) before summing, so the sum is multiplied by the number of reserve rows the claim has. Reproduce this, don't fix it.

columns.name: indemnity_reserve
columns.description: Latest INDEMNITY reserve on or before @AsOfDate. Ties on the date go to the highest reserve_id. 0 if none.

columns.name: expense_reserve
columns.description: Latest EXPENSE reserve on or before @AsOfDate, chosen the same way. 0 if none.

columns.name: incurred
columns.description: total_paid + current_reserve, including the inflated total_paid.

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.description: The @AsOfDate run parameter. Constant for the whole run.

defects.title: Payment/reserve join fan-out inflates total_paid and incurred
defects.description: #money LEFT JOINs stg.claim_payments and #reserve to #open_claims in one statement before GROUP BY. #reserve has up to one row per reserve type (INDEMNITY, EXPENSE), so every payment row is repeated once per reserve row and SUM(p.amount) is multiplied (typically doubled). COUNT(DISTINCT payment_id) and MAX(reserve) hide the fan-out, but total_paid, and therefore incurred (total_paid + reserves), are overstated.
defects.intended_behaviour: total_paid should be the plain sum of payments on or before @AsOfDate per claim, aggregated separately from the reserves (or pre-aggregated before joining).
defects.impact_query: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(amount) AS paid FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(g.total_paid - COALESCE(p.paid, 0))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claims_summary g LEFT JOIN p ON p.claim_id = g.claim_id WHERE g.total_paid <> COALESCE(p.paid, 0)

impact.query: WITH p AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(amount) AS paid FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(g.total_paid - COALESCE(p.paid, 0))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_claims_summary g LEFT JOIN p ON p.claim_id = g.claim_id WHERE g.total_paid <> COALESCE(p.paid, 0)

defects.title: claim_ref becomes NULL when handler_code is NULL
defects.description: claim_ref is built as lob_code + '/' + claim_number + '/' + handler_code. With SQL Server's default CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL, a NULL handler_code (an allowed value) makes the whole reference NULL, so the claim drops off the handler worklist reference.
defects.intended_behaviour: Build the reference with the handler part blank or defaulted (e.g. CONCAT or ISNULL(handler_code,'')), so LOB and claim number still appear.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_claims_summary g WHERE g.claim_ref IS NULL AND g.handler_code IS NULL

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_claims_summary g WHERE g.claim_ref IS NULL AND g.handler_code IS NULL

defects.title: Open book uses current status instead of status at the reporting date
defects.description: Claims are selected on today's status IN ('OPEN','REOPENED'), not on whether they were open at @AsOfDate. A claim notified by the reporting date but closed after it (closed_date > @AsOfDate) is left out of the as-of open book, along with its paid and reserves.
defects.intended_behaviour: Include claims open at @AsOfDate, i.e. reported on or before @AsOfDate and not closed by then (closed_date IS NULL OR closed_date > @AsOfDate).
defects.impact_query: WITH miss AS (SELECT claim_id FROM stg_claims WHERE reported_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' AND (status IS NULL OR UPPER(TRIM(status)) NOT IN ('OPEN','REOPENED')) AND closed_date > DATE'2025-12-31'), pay AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(amount) AS paid FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id), res AS (SELECT claim_id, reserve_type, reserve_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY claim_id, reserve_type ORDER BY reserve_date DESC, reserve_id DESC) AS rn FROM stg_claim_reserves WHERE reserve_date <= DATE'2025-12-31'), r AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(TRIM(reserve_type)) IN ('INDEMNITY','EXPENSE') THEN reserve_amount ELSE 0 END) AS resv FROM res WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(pay.paid, 0) + COALESCE(r.resv, 0))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM miss LEFT JOIN pay ON pay.claim_id = miss.claim_id LEFT JOIN r ON r.claim_id = miss.claim_id

impact.query: WITH miss AS (SELECT claim_id FROM stg_claims WHERE reported_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' AND (status IS NULL OR UPPER(TRIM(status)) NOT IN ('OPEN','REOPENED')) AND closed_date > DATE'2025-12-31'), pay AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(amount) AS paid FROM stg_claim_payments WHERE payment_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY claim_id), res AS (SELECT claim_id, reserve_type, reserve_amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY claim_id, reserve_type ORDER BY reserve_date DESC, reserve_id DESC) AS rn FROM stg_claim_reserves WHERE reserve_date <= DATE'2025-12-31'), r AS (SELECT claim_id, SUM(CASE WHEN UPPER(TRIM(reserve_type)) IN ('INDEMNITY','EXPENSE') THEN reserve_amount ELSE 0 END) AS resv FROM res WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY claim_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(pay.paid, 0) + COALESCE(r.resv, 0))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM miss LEFT JOIN pay ON pay.claim_id = miss.claim_id LEFT JOIN r ON r.claim_id = miss.claim_id

defects.title: Policy number taken from a single global snapshot date
defects.description: @snapshot_date is the latest snapshot date across all policies, and the policy join matches that exact date. A policy missing from that one snapshot (e.g. lapsed or not extracted that day) gets a NULL policy_number, even though an earlier snapshot on or before @AsOfDate holds it.
defects.intended_behaviour: Use each policy's own latest snapshot on or before @AsOfDate to get the policy number.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_claims_summary g WHERE g.policy_number IS NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stg_policy_snapshots ps WHERE ps.policy_id = g.policy_id AND ps.snapshot_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' AND ps.policy_number IS NOT NULL)

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_claims_summary g WHERE g.policy_number IS NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM stg_policy_snapshots ps WHERE ps.policy_id = g.policy_id AND ps.snapshot_date <= DATE'2025-12-31' AND ps.policy_number IS NOT NULL)

tests.description: Status filter (line 73) with case variants. 'open' and 'Reopened' match IN ('OPEN','REOPENED') under the CI collation, so legacy keeps them. A naive Spark isin drops them. Canonical OPEN/REOPENED rows and CLOSED/closed rows are on either side. Payments give the money columns values.

Status filter (line 73) with trailing spaces. 'OPEN ' and 'REOPENED  ' still match in SQL Server because trailing spaces are ignored. A naive Spark isin drops them. Canonical values are included, plus a leading-space ' OPEN' and a 'CLOSED ' that match in neither engine.

Latest-reserve pick (PARTITION BY reserve_type, lines 90-91) with case variants. Claim 301 has INDEMNITY 5000 (Jan) and a later 'Indemnity' 2000 (Jun). Legacy puts both in one partition and keeps only 2000. Spark splits them, keeps both, and MAX gives 5000. Claim 302 has the same pattern for EXPENSE/expense. Claim 303 has two canonical INDEMNITY rows, and 304 has no reserves.

Latest-reserve pick (lines 90-91) with trailing spaces. Claim 401 has EXPENSE 900 (Jan) and a later 'EXPENSE ' 400. Claim 402 has 'INDEMNITY ' 7000 (Feb) and a later INDEMNITY 2500. SQL Server puts each pair in one partition and keeps only the later amount. Spark splits them, and MAX picks the older, larger amount. Claim 403 is a canonical control.

Indemnity pivot (line 106) with case variants. Claims 501 and 502 have a single 'Indemnity' and 'indemnity' reserve. Legacy counts them as INDEMNITY. A case-sensitive Spark CASE gives 0. Claim 503 uses the canonical INDEMNITY, and 504 has only EXPENSE.

Indemnity pivot (line 106) with trailing spaces. 'INDEMNITY ' and 'INDEMNITY   ' equal 'INDEMNITY' in SQL Server, so they count. A naive Spark equality gives 0. Claim 603 uses the canonical value as a control.
Expense pivot (line 107) with case variants. 'Expense' and 'expense' reserves count as EXPENSE under the CI collation. A case-sensitive Spark CASE gives 0. Claim 703 uses the canonical EXPENSE.
Expense pivot (line 107) with trailing spaces. 'EXPENSE ' and 'EXPENSE  ' match 'EXPENSE' in SQL Server. A naive Spark equality gives 0. Claim 803 uses the canonical value as a control.

claim_ref built with + (line 136). Claims 902 and 904 have a NULL handler_code, so legacy claim_ref is NULL. concat_ws or coalescing to '' would give 'MOT/CLM902/' instead. The other claims have handlers. Lower-case and padded lob_code values also exercise the UPPER/RTRIM.

loss_date_text from CONVERT style 103 (line 143), which gives dd/mm/yyyy with leading zeros. Loss dates include single-digit day and month (2025-03-04, 2025-01-09), a day over 12 (2024-11-25) and day=month (2025-07-07). The mix catches dd/MM vs MM/dd swaps, missing padding, or ISO default formatting.

reported_period from CONVERT(CHAR(6), d, 112) (line 145): yyyymmdd cut to yyyymm. Reported dates cover single-digit months, December, a leap day and a year boundary. The mix catches yyyy-MM, yyyyMMdd, or a missing zero pad on the month.

days_open = DATEDIFF(DAY, reported_date, @AsOfDate) (line 146). Spark's datediff(end, start) takes its arguments in the reverse order, so swapping them gives negative values. Reported dates include the as-of date itself (0 days), the day before, a leap-year span and a multi-year span. Claim 1206 is reported after the as-of date and is filtered out.

warnings: lineage agent notes: 1) Possible legacy bug (row fan-out): #money LEFT JOINs both claim_payments and #reserve on claim_id before GROUP BY (lines 109-115). A claim can have up to two reserve rows (INDEMNITY and EXPENSE), so SUM(p.amount) counts each payment once per reserve row, and total_paid and incurred can come out doubled. The migration must reproduce this behaviour to match the legacy output; n_payments is not affected because it uses COUNT(DISTINCT). 2) claim_ref is NULL whenever handler_code is NULL, because string concatenation with + returns NULL by default (CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL). 3) policy_number comes from the single latest snapshot_date on or before @AsOfDate across the whole table, picked into the variable @snapshot_date (lines 121-123). If a policy is missing from that snapshot, policy_number is NULL; the job does not fall back to an earlier snapshot. 4) Reserve types other than INDEMNITY or EXPENSE are dropped, and the reserve_date filter only changes the reserve values, not which claim rows appear. 5) The PARTITION BY claim_id, reserve_type in the reserve ROW_NUMBER is listed as a ranks edge with lower confidence (0.6). 6) The joins to #money and #reserve keep every open claim, so the output has one row per claim from stg.claims that passes the filters on lines 73-74.

warnings:
translator notes: Things a reviewer should check:
1) In the #reserve ROW_NUMBER, rows that tie on reserve_date DESC and reserve_id DESC are broken by _row_seq ascending. In the legacy engine that tie is non-deterministic.
2) @snapshot_date is built as a one-row aggregate joined to stg.policy_snapshots, so nothing is collected to the driver. If no snapshot falls on or before AsOfDate, the max is NULL and every policy_number is NULL, as in the legacy code. If one policy has more than one row on the same snapshot date, the output gets duplicate rows, which the legacy PRIMARY KEY would have rejected.
3) Text comparisons on status and reserve_type, and the reserve_type partition, use upper(rtrim(x)). The original values are still the ones written out.
4) In the Spark code, SUM and ISNULL give smaller decimal types (e.g. decimal(22,2)) than T-SQL's decimal(38,2). All values have scale 2, so the values are the same; the harness casts to decimal(14,2) on output.
5) The payment_date filter from the LEFT JOIN's ON clause is applied to the payments before the join. For a left join this gives the same result.
6) reported_period is always exactly 6 characters, so it needs no CHAR(6) padding.
